implementation_result.defect_confirmed_by_direct_inspection_fi: KERNEL_BUILDER OPENED the MT-113 frame before changing anything, rather than working from the report. Observed: the saved-search row reads "authentication middleware refactor across the workspace mt113-108112-1786047630197954500" and at the Find pane right edge only a bare "R" of Restore survives - Remove is not visible at all.
implementation_result.root_cause: find_in_files.rs:3858 laid out ui.label(&bm.label) FIRST inside a left-to-right ui.horizontal. The label is USER CONTENT and therefore unbounded - a saved search carries the operator whole query - so it consumed the full available width before either button was placed, pushing them past the pane edge.
implementation_result.why_this_needed_its_own_mt: Argus addressed and clicked Remove perfectly well - its AccessKit node existed and its action terminalized, which MT-113 proved. So an automated proof PASSED while a human operator could neither see nor reach the control. Automated terminality and human reachability diverged. That is exactly the class HBR-VIS exists to catch, and exactly why an Argus receipt cannot serve as this MT acceptance signal.
implementation_result.fix: Reserve the CONTROLS first against the row right edge with egui::Layout::right_to_left, adding Remove before Restore so it lands rightmost and the visual order [label ... Restore Remove] is preserved, then let the label truncate into the remaining width via egui::Label::truncate().

library_behaviour_verified_not_assumed.truncate_exists: Label::truncate() confirmed present at egui 0.33.3 src/widgets/label.rs:71. library_behaviour_verified_not_assumed.tooltip_correction: An explicit .on_hover_text(&bm.label) was written FIRST and then REMOVED after reading the egui source. Label::show_tooltip_when_elided defaults to TRUE (label.rs:42) and fires only when galley.elided (label.rs:283). The explicit call would have stacked a SECOND tooltip on the built-in one and popped a redundant tooltip on short labels that are not truncated at all. egui own doc example documents combining them as the way to show DIFFERENT text, which is not what this row wants. The built-in behaviour satisfies AC-119-2 more precisely: the untruncated query is recoverable EXACTLY when it is hidden.

pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.status: ATTEMPTED, PROVEN VACUOUS, AND DELETED RATHER THAN SHIPPED
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.what_was_tried: A library-level regression guard was written that renders the whole panel through find_in_files::show() inside a Ui constrained with set_max_width(420) and measures ui.min_rect().width(), first absolutely and then as a DIFFERENTIAL between a panel with no bookmarks and one carrying a long-labelled bookmark.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.why_it_was_withdrawn: IT COULD NOT FAIL. Non-vacuity was tested two ways and the guard stayed green under BOTH: first with .truncate() removed from the label, and then with the entire pre-fix layout restored (label added first inside a left_to_right row). A guard that stays green while the defect is reinstated is not a guard - it is a false assurance, and shipping it would have been the same vacuous-proof pathology this WP has repeatedly had to correct (MT-115 found four vacuous FR assertions; MT-020 had to make six dishonest tests honest).
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.root_cause_of_the_vacuity: Diagnosed rather than guessed. In a bare egui Context with no real screen rect, other Find-in-Files surfaces - the single-line status/receipt text and the results ScrollArea configured auto_shrink([false, false]) - report an enormous min_rect: the first absolute measurement returned 9984px inside a nominally 420px pane. The panel is therefore already effectively unbounded in that harness, so a roughly 600px bookmark row NEVER overflows regardless of layout, and no measurement taken at panel level can distinguish the fixed row from the broken one. set_max_width does not constrain those children.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.what_would_actually_work: A MOUNTED harness (egui_kittest, as PT-119-1 uses) where the pane has a real width, reading the Restore/Remove node bounds out of the AccessKit tree by author_id and asserting containment within the pane bounds - the same bounds data the MCP snapshot already exposes per author_id. That is a mounted-proof-shaped task, not a lib-unit-shaped one. Alternatively the row rendering could be extracted into a directly testable function, but that is a product refactor beyond a layout fix.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.honest_consequence: MT-119 therefore has NO automated regression guard. Its acceptance rests on PT-119-1, the mounted GPU frame that was captured and OPENED. The fix can silently regress between mounted runs until a mounted rect assertion exists. This is stated plainly rather than papered over with the green-but-meaningless test that was deleted.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.tree_state: The deleted test left NO residue: git diff against the committed fix fef0faa9 is empty, and cargo test --lib find_in_files is 46 passed / 0 failed. The temporary pre-fix edits used to test non-vacuity were reverted by targeted replacement - no reset, stash, checkout -- or clean was used on the shared branch.

pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.status: ATTEMPTED IN THE MOUNTED HARNESS AND ALSO WITHDRAWN - for a DIFFERENT and more important reason
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_was_tried: A geometry assertion inside the mounted proof (tests/test_author_id_budget.rs): read the Restore/Remove node bounds out of the argus.inspect() tree by author_id and assert their right edges lie within the pane, deriving the pane edge from sibling Find-in-Files controls that cannot legally sit outside their own pane.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_happened: It FIRED - reporting the Restore control right edge at 2605.875px against a derived pane edge of 1557.34px. That is a FALSE POSITIVE: 2605px lies beyond the ENTIRE 2560px harness window, and the GPU frame captured in the same run shows both controls comfortably inside the pane.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.root_cause: argus.inspect() calls HandshakeApp::capture_mcp_snapshot_for_navigation (app.rs:12159), which calls refresh_mcp_snapshot() - and that renders on a FRESH egui::Context. The bounds in the inspect tree therefore describe a SYNTHETIC re-render, not the mounted frame. They are not comparable to what the operator sees.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.why_this_finding_matters_beyond_mt119: This is the same fresh-context hazard already known to make egui::Memory-backed state (popups, context menus) read back EMPTY - but its consequence for BOUNDS was not previously recorded. Any MT that tries to assert geometry, containment, clipping or overlap from the inspect tree will get answers that do not describe the rendered UI. That directly affects HBR-VIS style acceptance and MT-108 pixel gates.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_would_actually_work: Geometry must be measured from the MOUNTED egui pass - for example by having the product expose the rendered rects, or by asserting against the captured frame itself - not from the MCP snapshot tree.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.discipline_note: The assertion was NOT loosened to make it pass. Loosening a threshold until a false positive goes quiet would have fabricated a green with no meaning - the same failure as the vacuous lib-level guard deleted earlier. It was reverted and the finding recorded instead.

scope.summary: Bound the saved-search row layout so an unbounded user query cannot push its Restore and Remove controls outside the Find-in-Files pane.

observed_defect.symptom: The saved-search row renders the FULL UNTRUNCATED query as its label. With a realistic long query this pushes the Restore/Remove controls past the pane right edge: only "Re..." of Restore remains visible and Remove is clipped ENTIRELY off-pane.
observed_defect.why_it_is_not_caught_by_argus: This is the subtle part. Argus addresses and clicks Remove FINE - the AccessKit node exists and its action terminalizes correctly, which is exactly what MT-113 proved. So an automated proof passes while a HUMAN OPERATOR CANNOT SEE OR REACH the control. Automated terminality and human reachability diverge here, which is precisely the class of defect HBR-VIS exists to catch.
observed_defect.relationship_to_mt113: Same root pathology - unbounded user content in a bounded surface - but in the LAYOUT dimension rather than the identity dimension. MT-113 bounded the author_id; nothing bounds the rendered label.

acceptance_criteria: AC-119-1: with a query long enough to overflow the row, BOTH Restore and Remove render FULLY INSIDE the Find-in-Files pane at the tested viewport. Prove it by OPENING the frame and describing what is visible, not merely by capturing it.

AC-119-2: the full query text remains RECOVERABLE by the operator (elide with a tooltip, wrap, or an equivalent affordance). Truncating the label so the operator can no longer tell two saved searches apart is NOT an acceptable fix.
AC-119-3: the AccessKit author_ids and the MT-113 bounded identities are UNCHANGED - this is a layout fix only. Re-run the MT-113 proofs and show them still green.
AC-119-4: check the same overflow class on the other Find-in-Files rows (result rows, bookmark headings) and either fix them or record explicitly that they were checked and are safe.
